Cautiously positive overall, but further tempered by the August 2017 Beige Book. While the FOMC highlights solid job gains and begins balance sheet normalization, the Beige Book points to only modest-to-moderate growth and subdued price pressures, consistent with below-target inflation. It also documents hurricane-related disruptions—especially along the Gulf Coast and in the Dallas and Atlanta Districts—affecting the energy and natural resources sector (including Eagle Ford) and creating mixed agricultural conditions. These near-term headwinds, alongside July SLOOS reports of softer demand across CRE and consumer loans and some tighter consumer standards (with mortgage easing partially offsetting), reinforce the Committee’s gradualism and reduce the hawkish tilt implied by labor strength and normalization. On net, the Beige Book’s disruption and modest inflation tone warrant a slight downgrade from the initial assessment.
